finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into the SQL string via an f-string. An attacker can break out of the LIKE literal and run UNION SELECT queries to read any table in shop.db, including columns not exposed by the API such as price or owner, and any other tables in the database.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term = request.args.get('q', '') taken from the query string with no validation
term is interpolated directly into the SQL text with an f-string, not bound as a parameter
Query results are returned to the caller as JSON, so UNION-based injection exfiltrates data directly

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, escaping or parameterization. No authentication or authorization decorators on the route. No WAF or middleware in the app. The other two routes (/product, /by-owner) use ? placeholders, so only /search is affected. sqlite3 execute() rejects stacked statements, so the impact is read/exfiltration through UNION or boolean injection rather than stacked writes.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 takes q unvalidated and app.py:12 f-string-interpolates it into the SQL with no auth, allowlist or parameterization, and app.py:13 returns rows as JSON so UNION injection exfiltrates data (the other routes at app.py:18 and :25 use ? placeholders).
